# Issue review

## Scope

The v0.2.0 triage of 2026-10-19: 17 open tasks, [[MAIN-125]], [[MAIN-129]] and [[MAIN-131]] to [[MAIN-145]] — milestone 3 without its two closed tasks, the Formula retirement and the tap publication through the App. The question is what must land before v0.2.0 ships directly as a stable release, without a release candidate. A finding blocks the tag only if shipping without it causes irreversible harm to user data, a compatibility trap, a security exposure, a release that cannot be published correctly, or a headline `fetch`/`status` scenario that fails for an ordinary user or is documented beyond what the binary does.

**Slice.** `main` at `73fb3d4`, clean working tree. The infrastructure port (`fee2d70` to `73fb3d4`) landed while the triage ran; it does not touch the Go code (`git diff --stat 12e08e1 73fb3d4 -- internal main.go main_test.go go.mod go.sum` is empty), so every claim about Go code holds on `73fb3d4`. Lines of the guides and the pipeline are cited at their position on `73fb3d4`.

**How the verdicts were reached.** Two independent passes over the same tasks and the same bar: `claude-opus-5.5-high`, with two forks of the same key for the guides against the CLI and for the release pipeline, and `gpt-6-astra-high`. A second round gave each pass the seven points on which they disagreed, to be decided again from the code, against its own earlier view where the code said so. This review consolidates both rounds, re-reads every `file:line` it cites on `73fb3d4` and reruns nine reproductions ([Validation and sources](#validation-and-sources)); the disagreements and how they were settled are in [Differences between the two passes](#differences-between-the-two-passes). The owner's decisions of 2026-10-19 are recorded per task in the column Release: `v0.2.0`, or `patch` — a v0.2.x patch after v0.2.0.

The state of the code lives here; the task bodies keep intent. Not looked at: the closed tasks of milestone 3 ([[MAIN-127]], [[MAIN-130]]), other milestones, a real publication, `fetch --apply` against GitHub.

### MAIN-129. Additive pinned adoption

- `planPinned` sets `UpdateRemote` whenever the observed origin differs from the canonical URL (`internal/service/fetch/pinned.go:84`) and still plans `adopt` (`:86-87`); the applier calls `UpdateRemote` before it records the adoption (`applier.go:43-48`).
- Close call in both passes: the hidden origin change breaks the additive model, but it deletes no work by itself; with B3 of [[MAIN-135]] it rewrites the whole Git configuration of the pin. `fetch.md:160-163` already says that a rename or transfer updates the origin of a pin, so no claim of the guide is broken.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch.

### MAIN-131. Exit codes of usage errors

- Reproduced (this review): `maintainer fecth` exits 0; `fetch --concurrency=abc` and `status --concurrency=abc` exit 1.
- `main.go:60-67` maps any error without an exit code to 1, and cobra's flag and argument errors carry none. Fetch keeps the config value for a negative `--concurrency` (`internal/command/fetch/root.go:104-107`); status rejects it (`internal/command/status/root.go:40-41`).
- Found by the Opus pass: `fetch --format=jsno` falls back to the human output with exit 0 (`internal/service/fetch/reporter.go:38-41`), while status rejects an unknown format (`internal/command/status/root.go:37-38`). `main_test.go:20-25` asserts inside an `exit` stub that a successful `Execute` never calls, so the test passes without checking anything.
- The exit-code tables (`docs/content/fetch.md:297-300`, `status.md:225-227`) promise exit 2 for these cases.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch; the v0.2.0 guides describe the codes the release binary returns ([[MAIN-132]]).

### MAIN-133. Owners, profiles and adoption filters

- **Filters.** An untracked snapshot with one clone returns `adopt` (`internal/service/fetch/planner.go:288-299`) before `if filtered` (`:304-305`). A pin returns even earlier, through `planPinned` (`:240-250`), and a workspace pin at `:252-263`. Reproduced by the Opus pass: with `exclude_forks = true` an untracked fork checkout is adopted on the first apply and fetched on every later run; no command untracks it.
- **`--owner`.** `resolveProfiles` narrows the owners of discovery (`internal/command/fetch/profiles.go:48-54`). `confirm` re-verifies every authorised record that discovery did not return (`internal/service/fetch/service.go:394-417`), and existing workspace checkouts are confirmed by id (`:176-208`). Reproduced by the Opus pass: with profiles narrowed to `acme`, a tracked `other/tool` renamed to `other/tool2` is confirmed, moved, and its origin is rewritten. `--profile` adds no mutation of its own: a confirmation with the wrong profile becomes a conflict row or a `gone` that heals on the next full run.
- **Token fallback.** A record whose profile has no token is confirmed with the primary profile (`service.go:402-405`), so a 404 from another token can be recorded as `gone`.
- **Case.** The allowlist is an exact map (`internal/service/github/discovery_rest.go:101-104`), and the endpoint choice compares the login exactly (`:122`). Per the Opus pass, `OctoLab` against the API's `octolab` discovers nothing, and a private organisation falls back to the public listing.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch for the code — the narrowing table, the filter on every adoption path including pins, the case-insensitive comparison, the profile-owned 404. The help, the guide and the template describe v0.2.0 in [[MAIN-132]].

### MAIN-134. Discovery failures and rate limits

- The scan resolves each GitHub checkout by name; any resolver error except a 404 is returned (`internal/service/fetch/adopter.go:127-130`; a 404 becomes id 0 at `service.go:565-566`), and `ScanScoped` fails the run (`service.go:150-153`). Per the Opus pass: a 401, 403 or 451 for one checkout of an SSO-protected or IP-allowlisted organisation fails every fetch, loudly and naming the repository. Moving that checkout out of the layout works around it; an `ignore` rule does not, because `Ignored` is consulted only after the scan (`service.go:178`).
- `RateGuard.shouldRetry` (`internal/service/github/rate.go:89-100`) retries a 403 only when the remaining quota is 0, and a 429 by `Retry-After` or backoff (`:151`). The secondary-limit, budget and permanent-error cases of the body were not re-run.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch. Planning stops before any mutation, so nothing is lost.

### MAIN-135. Checkout identity

- **B3, the origin update.** `UpdateRemote` (`internal/service/git/sync.go:147-174`) sets origin's URL in the typed and the raw config and calls `repo.SetConfig(cfg)` (`:170`), which serialises every section again. go-git v5.19.3 folds each remote's `pushurl` values into `URLs` (`config/config.go:669-670`) and writes that slice, or the saved original URLs when an `insteadOf` rule applied, back as `url` (`:677-691`); its decoder drops the bare-key flag, and its encoder always writes `key = value`. Reproduced by the Opus pass with the real `UpdateRemote`: another remote's `pushurl = DISABLE` gains `url = DISABLE`; a bare `[commit] gpgsign` is written as `gpgsign = `, which Git reads as false (this review: `true` against `false`), so commit signing silently turns off; full-line and inline comments disappear; with a repository-local `insteadOf`, origin is not updated, the call returns nil, and `no_push` is added to `remote.origin.url`. The origin push lock survives; `sync_test.go:138` covers origin only. The paths are a move with a remote update and `update_remote` (`planner.go:384-393`) and a pinned adoption (`pinned.go:84`). None of these patterns is in the owner's 162 checkouts; an ordinary user with an `upstream` remote whose push is disabled is exposed on the rename and transfer path, and a later patch cannot restore the comments or the booleans.
- **Name reuse.** Reproduced by the Opus pass: a record of id 1 at `public/acme/old` with a local branch `work`; id 1 is renamed to `acme/new`, and a new id 2 takes `acme/old`. The first apply adopts the checkout as id 2 — the name lookup wins (`adopter.go:122-124`), and adoption does not check which id the state attributes to that path (`planner.go:288-299`) — and clones id 1 fresh into `acme/new`, dropping its `previous_paths` (`:324-351`). The second apply fetches repository 2 into the checkout: `origin/master` follows unrelated history, and `work` is ahead 2, behind 1. The local work survives; the binding is wrong and stays wrong. `planPinned` lacks the same guard.
- Case-only renames and the order of move and remote update were not reproduced; per the Opus pass they fail as conflicts or do what a plain `git fetch` would.
- The parallel task of the fix confirmed the move order: after a successful move and a failed remote update, the state stays at the old path (`internal/service/fetch/applier.go:79-97`).
- Release: B3 is the only code blocker of v0.2.0; a parallel task fixes it and wrote its requirement into the body. The rest goes to a patch, split off as [[MAIN-150]]; see [The split of MAIN-135](#the-split-of-main-135).

### MAIN-136. Same-run refresh

- `Execute` performs one action per repository (`internal/service/fetch/applier.go:40-42`); the passes of `apply` have no dependent fetch (`service.go:420-483`). The guide keeps the second invocation (`fetch.md:172`, `:328`).
- Release: a v0.2.x patch by the owner's decision, which settles the scope freeze of [[MAIN-138]].

### MAIN-137. State selection and uncertain records

- Reproduced (this review): `state prune` drops a record under a `chmod 000` directory and exits 0 — `afero.Exists` returns an error that `state.go:54` discards. With `MAINTAINER_FETCH_CONFIG` set, `--config=""` shows the configured store, because `openState` sets `ExplicitSet: opts.config != ""` (`internal/command/fetch/state.go:83`), while `fetch` asks `cmd.Flags().Changed("config")` (`root.go:135`). Intermediate saves are discarded (`internal/service/fetch/service.go:453`, `:472`); the final save is returned (`:256`).
- What a lost record costs (the passes disagreed): a record carries the pin, the previous paths, the timestamps and the remote observations (`internal/state/state.go:20-40`). An in-layout checkout is adopted again with the same id, resolved from GitHub, not relocated — relocation needs a record (`planner.go:324-333`). The persisted pin is gone: per the Opus pass, a name-based pin, a rename and a pruned record together plan a duplicate clone at the layout path, visible in the plan, nothing deleted. While the path stays unreadable, fetch fails before any mutation.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch. No checkout is touched; the record cannot be rebuilt from the disk.

### MAIN-139. Prereleases out of stable channels

- No `prerelease: auto` or tap skip in `release:` (`.goreleaser.yml:91-96`), so a suffixed tag would become *Latest* and update both tap files. A stable v0.2.0 wants exactly that; the release guide forbids prerelease tags until this task is closed.
- The second requirement checks `permissions.push` of a token. Since [[MAIN-140]], `cd` and `doctor` mint a tap-scoped `contents: write` token from the App (`.github/workflows/cd.yml:54-60`, `doctor.yml:52-58`), and minting fails without that access. The requirement's goal — a read must not pass for the ability to publish — is met another way. By the coordinator's decision the requirement is rewritten for the App token, not dropped: the mint step proves the right to write, and `permissions.push` of a personal token is no longer checked.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch; not a gate of v0.2.0.

### MAIN-140. Tap through the App

- `cd.yml:44-50` checks the App secrets in the preflight, `:54-60` mints a token scoped to `homebrew-tap` with `permission-contents: write`, `:114` hands it to GoReleaser; `.goreleaser.yml:17-18` and `:46-47` set `use_github_app_token: true`; `doctor.yml:52-58` mints the same way. No step reads `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`.
- Open: whether the Formula commit is verified like the Cask's, the App's access on a real push, and the revocation of the old token — all after the first release.
- Release: v0.2.0, milestone 3, by the coordinator's decision: its remaining criteria are proved by the v0.2.0 publication.

### MAIN-141. Distinct status rows

- `Collect` counts duplicates by the lower-cased display name over every row (`internal/service/status/service.go:161-165`), orphans and checkouts without a GitHub identity included. Reproduced by the Opus pass: two local-only repositories `alice/tool` and `bob/tool` become two error rows, exit 1. The broken-repository message blames `git config`.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch; `status.md:145-147` and `:157` say more than v0.2.0 does ([[MAIN-132]]).

### MAIN-142. Counters on re-inspection

- `Inspect` adds to the counters of the row it is given (`internal/service/status/git.go:168-173`, `:201`, `:209`); `Collect` builds a fresh row per checkout (`service.go:128-143`), so no caller sees it today.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch.

### MAIN-143. Summary and selection

- The plain header prints the number of checkouts only (`internal/service/status/view.go:125`). `rebuild` takes the anchor's index among the filtered rows and falls back to 0 (`terminal.go:76-79`), so sorting under a filter that hides the anchor moves the highlight; `status.md:133-134` promises that sorting preserves the selection.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch.

### MAIN-144. Workspace boundaries

- Reproduced by the Opus pass with the default layout `{{.Visibility}}/{{.Owner}}/{{.Repo}}` and `root/public/acme` symlinked outside the root: apply cloned `acme/svc` outside and moved a tracked `old/tool`, transferred to `acme`, out of the root as well. Nothing was lost; the files sit where the user's symlink points. Every later run reports both as conflicts with exit 3, and status no longer lists them, because discovery does not follow symlinks (`internal/service/workspace/scope.go:133-138`, documented at `workspace.md:44`). No configuration is needed, only a directory symlink at the visibility or the owner level.
- The code path: occupancy checks only the final path (`internal/service/fetch/occupancy.go:29`), clone creates the parents through the symlink (`internal/service/git/sync.go:35`), and move creates and renames through it (`:128-137`). Collisions compare exact destination strings (`planner.go:472`); overlapping destinations need owner templates of different depth. A clone into an existing ancestor is refused (`sync.go:41-46`); one into a descendant nests a repository.
- A `.git` at the owner level hides the checkouts below it: `status` prints `[]` and exits 0 (Opus pass).
- Release: a v0.2.x patch.

### MAIN-145. Pins with sufficient context

- A matching rule renders from the snapshot it receives (`internal/service/fetch/pinned.go:10-17`); the persisted pins of the records are rendered from `{id, owner, name}` alone (`service.go:140`). The current rule already precedes the persisted `pinned_path` (`pinned.go:11-20`). Reproduced by the Opus pass on a templated id-only pin: `status` shows an error row instead of an unresolved pin. Identity checks keep a wrong render from adopting an arbitrary checkout; the owner's four pins are literal paths.
- Release: a v0.2.x patch.

#### F1. The state temporary file follows a symlink

- `Store.Save` writes `<state>.tmp` with `afero.WriteFile` (`internal/state/store.go:117-118`), which opens it with `O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_TRUNC` (afero v1.15.0 `ioutil.go:125-126`), then `Chmod`s and renames it (`store.go:121-126`). A link planted under that fixed name is followed: reproduced here and by the Opus pass, the link's target gets the state JSON and mode 0600, and `state.json` becomes a symlink to the target. Every save, `state prune` included, does it.
- Exposure: the default state directory is created 0700 (`store.go:114`, `:134`), so only the same user or root can plant the link there. A custom `state_file` in a shared directory makes it reachable; no guide suggests one.
- The gpt-6-astra pass rated it a P0 blocker at first and withdrew that in the second round; the Opus pass rated it a P2 hardening. The owner: a patch — exotic, but the finding stays recorded.

#### F2. Moving a checkout breaks its linked worktrees

- A move is an `os.Rename` of the checkout (`internal/service/git/sync.go:137`). The `.git` file of each linked worktree still names the old `…/.git/worktrees/<name>`, so Git refuses to work there: `fatal: gitfile does not point to a valid repository`. `git worktree repair`, run in the moved checkout, restores the links. Nothing is lost.
- The plan does not say that a moved checkout has linked worktrees, and the apply does not repair them. Milestone 3 lists linked worktrees as out of scope as a feature to manage; this is about a move not breaking them.
- The other direction, found by the executor of the `UpdateRemote` fix: `Inspect` opens a checkout with go-git `PlainOpen` (`internal/service/git/sync.go:177-186`), which does not set `EnableDotGitCommonDir` (go-git v5.19.3 `repository.go:304-334`). For a checkout that is itself a linked worktree it reads the worktree's own Git directory instead of the main repository's configuration, which `git config --local` reads and the fixed `UpdateRemote` writes. Reproduced here with a probe on go-git v5.19.3: for a linked worktree `w` of a repository with an origin, `git -C w config --local remote.origin.url` prints the URL, `PlainOpen(w)` sees no origin, and `PlainOpenWithOptions(w, EnableDotGitCommonDir)` sees it; for the main repository both see it.

#### F3. An interrupted clone is adopted as a checkout

- A clone that fails after it started keeps the partial checkout for inspection: `cloneFailure` removes only an empty reserved directory (`internal/service/git/sync.go:68-79`). Per the Opus pass, a clone cut by `--timeout` or a signal leaves a repository with an origin and no checked-out commit, and the next run adopts it like any other checkout (`planner.go:288-299`), so status shows it as `unborn`. Recoverable by removing it and cloning again, or by fetching and checking out by hand.
- Not reproduced here: it needs an interrupted network clone.

#### F4. The help says "It never deletes"

- `maintainer fetch --help` says "It never deletes" (`internal/command/fetch/root.go:45-47`), while every fetch prunes remote-tracking refs (`internal/service/git/sync.go:111-115`) and `state prune` forgets records. [[MAIN-132]] already rewrites the guide's wording ("existing checkouts and local work are retained"); the help follows it there, under the owner's decision that the help is true for the release. The Opus pass rated it a P3 wording fix.

#### F5. Unknown configuration keys are accepted silently

- `LoadFetch` decodes TOML and YAML into the structure without rejecting unknown keys (`internal/config/fetch.go:138`, `:145`). Reproduced here: a profile with `include_owner = ["acme"]` validates as `ok … (1 profiles, 0 owners, …)`, exit 0. An omitted `include_owners` means "you and every organisation you are a member of" (`fetch.md:117`, `internal/config/fetch_template.go:31`), so the typo widens discovery; plan mode shows the wider plan before anything is applied.
- Owner's decision: not a compatibility trap. A key outside the schema never worked, so rejecting it makes the implicit contract explicit; the fix rejects unknown keys and keeps a CUE schema next to the config.

### The split of MAIN-135

Done after the parallel task wrote the origin requirement into [[MAIN-135]]. [[MAIN-135]] keeps only that requirement — `UpdateRemote` changes only `remote.origin.url` and verifies it; other remotes, bare booleans, comments and a repository-local `insteadOf` survive — under the title "fetch: remote: change only the origin URL when updating a remote", and stays in milestone 3, to be closed by the fix. [[MAIN-150]], for a v0.2.x patch, carries the rest under the old title: a recorded checkout is never rebound to another id (also on the pinned path and over `previous_paths`), case-only renames, the move committed to state before the remote update, and the metadata refresh after a fetch, with this review's name-reuse reproduction as its PoC. The unpublished local note of 2026-10-01 moved with the identity work to [[MAIN-150]].
